verdict: This is the strongest-shaped pick on the board and I would lean forward: 4.2 is the one statement where the 3D is literally M2, every visual element described is driven by the data or the simulator (heat = pick counts, routes = Held-Karp on the aisle graph, counters = the same per-order metres the worker scored), the evaluation is honest by construction (one pure simulate(), time-split held-out, eval script with commit hash, no backend to go down), and the Ghost Race is a genuinely memorable way to render "replay the same orders before and after" that no other team will think of. All three must-haves are met as written and all three watch-outs are addressed. What stops it being a 9 as drafted: the signature race, as scripted, beats a seeded-random "original" layout, so the dramatic -20.8% is the automatic baseline's win dressed up as the player's; the honest comparison (baseline vs player/SA) will be a few percent and visually a near-tie, and the narration pre-commits to "the annealer beats the ABC baseline" before any number exists. Second, the scene is over-specified against the "simple geometry, average laptop" watch-out (Bloom + N8AO + SMAA + 2048 shadow maps + per-carton troika text + two skinned meshes) and the code volume (~3-4k LOC across R3F, post-processing, workers, SA, DP) strains the "every member explains every line" rule for a team that also has to sleep. Third, the 5-minute script packs six WOW moments, a live annealer run and an evidence tour with no slack; one stalled SA run or a mis-click in 3D under a projector costs the close. Fix the race semantics and the headline KPI, lock a Medium quality default, cut the decorative stack, and rehearse a deterministic hero invoice, and this wins the track.
fatal_flaws: Ghost Race strawman: as scripted (apply Baseline at 1:20, do 3-4 swaps, press RACE) the ghost is the seeded-random Original, so the -20.8% on screen is ~all baseline gain; 3-4 swaps out of 100 slots cannot move a month total by more than ~1%. The sharpest judge's first question is 'what is your gain over the baseline the statement told you to beat, on held-out?' and if the answer is ~2% and not on screen, the signature visual reads as theatre over a strawman. Must be fixed by racing explicitly labelled pairs (Original→Baseline, then Baseline→AI/You) and making held-out gain vs Baseline the headline KPI, not gain vs Original.
weaknesses: Pre-written narration assumes results ('annealer beats ABC because it co-locates co-picked products', 'baseline 25-40% below random, SA 3-10% below baseline'). With most covered orders having 1-5 lines in a 5-aisle grid with a corner dock, ABC/COI is near-optimal and SA may land at 0-3% on held-out or go negative after shrinkage; the 3:10-3:50 segment then has no point. Needs a Plan B narrative written now, not at 03:30.

SA wall-clock is unproven: plan claims 0.3-0.8 ms/move, but a swap re-routes every order containing either SKU (~100-240 orders) and even tiny Held-Karps in JS at 5-30 us each give 0.5-5 ms/move; 30k iterations is 15-150 s, versus a 40 s demo budget. Live run may finish mid-anneal on stage.

Baseline leakage: JSON skus[].picks is whole-month; if 'fast movers nearest dock' sorts on full-month picks while SA tunes on Nov 1-15 only, the baseline sees held-out data and the SA-vs-baseline held-out comparison is unfair in the baseline's favour. Must emit picks_opt and picks_all and sort the baseline on picks_opt.

Violates the spirit of watch-out 3 ('keep geometry simple'): N8AO half-res + Bloom + SMAA + 2048 shadow map + 15 emissive lamps + troika per-carton labels + 2 skinned meshes. '60 fps on Iris Xe at dpr 1.25 in High' is optimistic; Auto fallback measured over 90 frames after load happens while assets are still decoding, so it may misjudge. Judges may also open the URL on their own laptops.

Dark palette (#0b0f1a floor, bloom highlights) on a venue projector with ambient light becomes a black rectangle with cyan smears; also compresses badly in the 1080p30 recording and the YouTube cut. No 'projector' preset exists.

Explainability volume: ~3-4k LOC spanning R3F 9 / drei Instances / CameraControls / postprocessing / Web Worker protocol / zustand / Held-Karp bitmask DP / SA with inverted-index delta / Clarke-Wright batching. Four humans who also sleep and rehearse cannot narrate all of that; instructions make it a disqualification axis, not a nice-to-have.

Both rack sides share one access node, so 100 slots are really 50 distinct positions for distance purposes; swapping across the aisle is a no-op and a judge who tries it will see the counter not move. Must be visible in the UI (pairs shown as one bay) or explained before asked.
Click-to-swap on 1.2 m cartons from the Overview camera on a trackpad under projector zoom is fiddly; the robust 2D SlotPanel is parked as a stretch goal rather than the demo path.

Demo script is over-dense: six WOWs, three mode switches with 0.6-2.5 s camera transitions, a live SA run, an evidence tour, a stretch tour and QR codes in 300 s; narration as written is ~450 words (~3.5 min at 130 wpm) before any interaction latency. Zero slack for a stall or a judge question mid-demo.

Coverage honesty is only a global chip; each replayed order silently drops its non-top-100 lines, so the twin replays a fraction of every real invoice. The judge who asks 'what fraction of this order did I just watch?' gets no on-screen answer.
Random 'Original' (seed 42) is a weak reference; a catalogue-order original (slots in StockCode order, which is what many real warehouses look like) costs one line and is harder to call a strawman.

Kenney URL in the plan (kenney.nl/assets/mini-characters-1) is a 404; the real page is kenney.nl/assets/mini-characters (CC0, 25 files, 'Animation' feature tag) and the GLB clip names/formats are unverified. The procedural fallback exists but the plan should time-box the GLB to 45 min.

Pick-time metric is affine in distance (m/1.2 + 10 s x lines), so the 'average pick time per order' column carries no information beyond the km column; a judge may ask why both are shown as if independent.
Integration window 05:00-07:00 'with a human' assumes an awake human at 5 am after a 22:00-04:30 build; the 23:30 walking skeleton is the only early checkpoint before a long dark gap.
fixes: Race semantics: the ghost is always the layout the player started this session from, labelled on screen ('Ghost: Baseline (fast movers)'). Demo runs two races: Original→Baseline (big visible gap, narrated as the automatic baseline's win) then Baseline→AI(SA) or Baseline→You (small gap, narrated as 'this is the part the statement asked us to beat'). KPI card headline = held-out gain vs Baseline; gain vs Original shown secondary.

Pick a deterministic hero invoice (by id, at 1x, follow-cam, split dual follow-cams or fitToBox on both pickers) where the per-order Original-vs-Baseline gap is large, rehearse the exact pause moment, then switch to 20x overview for the month sweep with diverging counters.

SA runtime gate at 02:00: log us/move in the worker; if >0.6 ms, the live button runs a 10 s capped 'sprint' (iterations shown) and the 30k-iteration result from `npm run eval` ships as the 'AI (SA, 30k iters, precomputed by npm run eval, commit X)' row. Never let the demo wait on an unfinished anneal.

Write the SA Plan-B narration now: 'SA finds X% in-sample but only Y% held-out — the baseline is already near-optimal for small orders; the affinity gain lives in multi-line orders (show that subset row).' Publish whatever lands.
Emit picks_opt and picks_all per SKU in the JSON; baseline sorts on picks_opt; heat colours use picks_opt; Evidence tab states this in one line.

Quality: default = Medium (Bloom only, no N8AO, no shadow maps, dpr <=1.25, no troika labels except hovered carton); High = opt-in; Auto probe starts after useGLTF/useProgress reports 100%. Drop n8ao from the stack entirely unless fps >=55 on the oldest team laptop by 10:00. Add a 'Projector' preset: floor #1a2030, hemisphere 1.0, route lineWidth 5, counters 56 px, vignette off.

Scope cuts to protect explainability (target <=2,800 LOC app code): drop DragControls, largestGap, per-carton troika labels, two-picker congestion; keep batch picking only if <=150 LOC; one owner per module writes a 10-line 'how it works' in DEV_LOG; 11:00-11:30 explain-it-back session, delete anything nobody can narrate.

Promote the 2D SVG SlotPanel (10x10 grid mirroring heat colours, click-click swap) to a must-ship demo control; 3D click-to-swap stays as the showpiece with a large hover halo and bay-level hit targets (raycast against bay boxes, not 1.2 m cartons).

Order card shows 'k of n lines in this zone' per invoice; Evidence tab shows a histogram of covered lines per order and median stops per order, so coverage honesty is per-order and pre-empts the question.
Add 'Original (catalogue order)' as the default Original and keep 'Original (random, seed 42)' as a second row; declare both in README.

Trim the script: Evidence = 20 s (one sentence + table already on screen), stretch = 15 s only if green on the live URL, end on the Baseline→AI race frame with the held-out table beside it; narration <=400 words; two timed rehearsals by 12:30 with a non-operator holding the clicker.

Fix the asset URL to https://kenney.nl/assets/mini-characters and verify GLB clip names in the first 30 min of Agent B; if no walk clip in GLB, go straight to the procedural capsule + cart (bob 2 Hz) and do not return.

Expose the shared-access-node simplification in the UI: render the two sides of a bay as one selectable bay pair, or state 'both sides of a bay share one walk point' in the Assumptions tab and the swap hint.

Make the hourly-commit evidence robust: humans merge agent branches at :00 with conventional messages; eval/results.md regenerated and committed at 03:30, 07:00 and 11:00 so numbers in README, deck and posts all trace to the 11:00 commit hash.
steal_worthy: Evaluation rendered as theatre: two agents on identical inputs (ghost = before, solid = after) with diverging counters — portable to 3.2 (uncontrolled vs scheduled load curves racing), 4.3 (pre- and post-disruption routes), 2.1 (shift plans).
One pure, seedless simulate() shared by the Web Worker scorer, the eval script and the animation, with 'press Replay twice, same numbers' as the honesty demo.
Time-split held-out with in-sample vs held-out shrinkage printed side by side as the honesty signal, plus an in-app Evidence tab showing the exact command and commit hash that produced the numbers.
Annealer cinema: streaming accepted moves from a worker as throttled animations with energy sparkline, temperature and seed on screen — turns optimisation into a watchable segment.
Zero-backend static deploy with every asset self-hosted (fonts, model, JSON), CDN mirror and local preview as fallbacks — the demo cannot be killed by venue Wi-Fi or a cold start.
Quality Auto mode with a post-load frame-timing probe and PerformanceMonitor dpr stepping; a 'Projector' colour preset.
Pre-processing meta block with logged removal counts (C-invoices, non-positive, non-product codes) surfaced in-app so watch-outs are visibly satisfied.
